questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: the city and the language was the main aspects. However I also found the main building of the university and the course selection very interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy and the UNi vien international office and the erasmus team was very helpfull.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Help with my course registration from the international office and mobility coordinator.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: WG- gesucht.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: just send a bunch of applications on WG-gesucht, then you will relatively easy find accomodation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The enrolment process was, from what I remember, relatively accessible and understandable, as it is all done via mobility online/digital.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Uni Wien international office, was always very helpfull to answer questions on email, and they would always reply back quickly.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The registration for classes was for me very difficult and confusing, due to the fact that it was very different from my home university and hence I had to have 10 courses in comparison to 2-3 courses. The system was not very user-friendly.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You'll need to spend some time familiarising yourself with which courses you can enrol in and what different types of courses there are: lecture, seminar, etc. as different courses have different attendance requirements and different types of exams. Therefore, it's always a good idea to take a mix.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: In general, the level at university was lower, a lot of one-way communication from the teacher towards the students and thus not much interaction, which I'm used to from my university back home.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In general, the level at courses was lower, not that much was expected from the students. The teaching consisted of a lot of one-way communication from the teacher towards the students and thus not much interaction, which I'm used to from my university back home.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At UCPH, teaching is more inclusive with the students, making it more interactive rather than passive, where you just have to listen to what a teacher reads out, which was the main style og teaching in Vienna

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries in Austria was more expensive than expected, however going out to eat and drink is less expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could sign up for dance classes, yoga classes, swimming, football, boxing, etc. I paid around 70 euros for a weekly Pilates class, which I was really happy about.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sports courses at UNI wien sport faculty and just all of the erasmus events.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on weekendtrips to Budapest, Prague, Bratislava, or travel within Austria to visit and explore the amazing nature. I went to Semmering an hour outside of Vienna, to do a longer hike, which i can definitely recommend.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It can be relatively difficult to get in touch with locals, as you'll mostly socialise with other Erasmus students. However, you may be lucky, especially if you take German language courses, to meet some locals. In addition, erasmus vienna has a buddy programme where you can be assigned a buddy who can help you with practical things, but also someone you can meet socially.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The formal way of approaching people is a thing that differs from Denmark. At uni you have to approach you teacher more formal and especially when you write emails etc.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Vienna is a very special city as it has so much history and culture, which was one of the reasons I chose to do an exchange programme there.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I chose to attend a German course in September that was organised by sprachenzentraum, which is part of the University of Vienna. As the semester doesn't start until October, it was a great opportunity to get to know the city, improve your German and meet some new people before starting your courses. If you pass the final German exam, you will be reimbursed up to 50-70 per cent of your course costs.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Familiarise yourself with all the practicalities in advance

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: For me it was also particularly special to go on exchange all by myself, to build a life in a foreign city without knowing anyone, but in the end having built up a large network, it was very rewarding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Creating a balance between studying and making new friends and exploring a new city and country.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
